headline: Approved $200,000 soil cleanup at 448 High Street, Comcast conduit at 75 Riverside Avenue, and $57,870 school repair funds.
summary: The meeting approved $200,000 for soil cleanup at 448 High Street and $45,470 for firefighter turnout gear. It also approved a Comcast conduit at 75 Riverside Avenue and moved $57,870 in school repair funds. Several items were referred to committees, including a draft ban on black plastic takeout containers and the sale of McCormick Avenue parcels.
decisions: Approved a resolution honoring the Congregational Church of West Medford Sanctuary UCC, 7-0.
Requested a cost report on longer vacation time for city employees and referred it to the Administration and Finance Committee, 7-0.
Approved a resolution supporting the Tufts resident assistants' union in its contract negotiations, 7-0.
Referred a request for a draft ordinance banning black plastic takeout containers to the Energy and Environment Committee, with a further referral to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee.
Referred a request for an administration update on the Veterans Department vacancy to the next regular meeting, 7-0.
Approved Comcast's grant of location for underground conduit and a manhole at 75 Riverside Avenue, 7-0.
Approved a common victualler license for Pavement Coffeehouse at 177 College Avenue, 7-0.
Referred the linkage fee ordinance update, including a new affordable housing fee, to the Community Development Board, 7-0.
Approved two $5,000 legal settlements, for Frank Pavaleo and Vivian Wright.
Approved $45,470 from the capital stabilization fund for firefighter turnout gear, 7-0.
Approved $200,000 from the capital stabilization fund for soil remediation at 448 High Street, 7-0.
Approved moving $57,870 from the Roberts Elementary repair project to the Missitug and Brooks Elementary repair projects, 7-0.
Referred the city charter implementation request to the Department of Elections and to the mayor, 7-0.
Referred the order to sell McCormick Avenue parcels to the Committee of the Whole, with amendments, 7-0.
Approved sending a comment letter to the MWRA Cambridge and Somerville combined sewer overflow project team, 6-1.
Tabled the funding request for the police chief search.
Approved cutting the law department's supplemental budget request and asking the mayor for an outside review of legal costs, 7-0.
Approved the September 15, 2026 board and commission appointments.
discussion: Members spoke in support of the Tufts resident assistants' bargaining. A union representative described proposed cuts to housing, meal swipes, and stipends, and asked for council support.

The McCormick Avenue parcels drew questions about why these lots were chosen, whether sale money would go to the affordable housing trust, and whether all unused city lots should be reviewed. A nearby resident raised concerns about notice, road access, and rock ledge.
Members discussed law department funding. They said requested reports and an outside legal review had not arrived, and some proposed cutting funds while keeping staff salaries.
Members discussed the city charter. A legal opinion said the charter took effect and that the city clerk and council must handle codification, and members called for a shared implementation plan.
Members debated the MWRA sewer overflow letter. Some wanted a stronger goal of no overflow, while an advisory board member urged focus on overall water quality and cost.
